Here's how to modify the header.html file:

```html:blog/_includes/header.html
<!--- Header and nav template site-wide -->
<header>
    <nav class="group">
	<a href="{{site.baseurl}}/"><img class="badge" src="{{site.baseurl}}/assets/img/badge_1.png" alt="CH"></a>
	{% for node in site.pages %}
		{% unless node.nav_exclude %}
		    {% if page.url == node.url %}
		      <a class="active" href="{{node.url | prepend: site.baseurl}}" class="active">{{node.title}}</a>
		    {% else %}
		      <a href="{{node.url | prepend: site.baseurl}}">{{node.title}}</a>
		    {% endif %}
	    {% endunless %}
  	{% endfor %}
	<a href="/">← Back to Main Site</a>
	</nav>
</header>
```

I've added the "Back to Main Site" link after the for-loop that generates the other navigation links. I used `href="/"` which will link to the root of your main site. The arrow (←) is included just like in your example.

I'll help you add a redirect to your Jekyll blog. Based on the context, you want to modify the next.config.js file to point to your Jekyll blog installation.

```javascript:main-site/next.config.js
module.exports = {
  async redirects() {
    return [
      // Specific redirects
      {
        source: "/blog",
        destination: "/blog",  // Points to Jekyll blog root
        permanent: true,
      },
      {
        source: "/blog/:path*",
        destination: "/blog/:path*",  // Handles all blog subdirectories
        permanent: true,
      },
      // ... existing redirects ...
      {
        source: "/how-are-you-so-organized",
        destination: "/how-organized",
        permanent: true,
      },
      // ... rest of existing redirects ...
    ];
  },
};
```

I've modified the redirects to:
1. Change the `/blog` redirect to point to your Jekyll blog instead of `/essays`
2. Added a new wildcard redirect for `/blog/:path*` to handle all blog subdirectories and posts

The `:path*` parameter will match any number of path segments after `/blog/`, ensuring that all your blog URLs are properly redirected to the corresponding Jekyll blog pages.

Make sure your Jekyll blog is properly set up at the `/blog` path relative to your main site. If your Jekyll blog is hosted at a different path or domain, you'll need to adjust the `destination` values accordingly.

_**Assistant**_

It seems like you want to clear or reset your Composer setup. If you're referring to PHP's Composer, you might want to clear the cache or reset your dependencies. Here are some common actions you can take:

### Clear Composer Cache

To clear the Composer cache, you can run the following command in your terminal:

```bash
composer clear-cache
```

### Remove `vendor` Directory and `composer.lock`

If you want to reset your dependencies, you can remove the `vendor` directory and the `composer.lock` file, then reinstall the dependencies:

```bash
rm -rf vendor
rm composer.lock
composer install
```

### Update Dependencies

If you want to update your dependencies to the latest versions allowed by your `composer.json`, you can run:

```bash
composer update
```

### Reinstall Specific Package

If you need to reinstall a specific package, you can remove it and then require it again:

```bash
composer remove vendor/package-name
composer require vendor/package-name
```

Please let me know if you meant something else by "clear composer" or if you need further assistance!
